accounts.name: payer_ata
docs: settle; finalize requires the payer's ATA and decides whether it can
take the refund.

accounts.name: treasury_usdc
docs: The treasury's USDC ATA, which takes a refund the payer's ATA can't.
Optional, so the common settle carries no extra key, and never
required writable here: it is one account for the whole protocol, and
a write lock on it in every settle would serialize them all. The
submitter reads the payer's ATA first and marks it writable only when
the ATA can't take the refund; it may always pass it read-only, and
resend it writable on TreasuryAccountNotWritable if the ATA changed in
between.

types.name: ClaimFields
docs: What the node claims for a ticket; the payer's ack signs its hash. Every
count is a u64, as Algorand's settle arguments and the receipt's fields
are, so any receipt a node signs folds into a claim.

fields.name: _retired_owed_vault_bump
docs: Retired with the owed vault: an undeliverable refund now goes to the
treasury, as on Algorand. Retired fields keep their bytes so every
later offset stays put on the clusters that already hold a Config.
Those Configs still hold the old values (devnet and testnet have this
bump and an arbiter set), so set_config zeroes every retired field
and a field later carved from them starts from zero.

fields.name: paused
docs: Algorand's `paused`: stops `open` and every registry write (creating
and updating operators and nodes, a node's URL and staging). It never
gates settles, unregisters or the admin's levers, so a pause never
strands escrow or stake.

fields.name: _retired_pause_registry
docs: Retired: one flag gates what Algorand's one flag gates.

fields.name: _retired_max_grace
docs: Retired: open takes any grace the node passes and any future
expires_at, as Algorand's does. The payer's offer check, not the
program, refuses a grace other than 0.

fields.name: default_grace
docs: The grace a ticket gets when open passes 0.

fields.name: _retired_max_ticket_lifetime
docs: Retired with max_grace.

fields.name: operator_stake
docs: Micro-USDC escrowed by create_operator, which covers its first node.

fields.name: node_stake
docs: Micro-USDC escrowed by create_node for every node after the first.

fields.name: next_operator_id
docs: Starts at 1: 0 stays the "unset" operator id, as on Algorand.

fields.name: admin
docs: Also resolves frozen tickets, as Algorand's admin does.

fields.name: _retired_arbiter
docs: Retired with the separate arbiter seat.

fields.name: treasury
docs: A wallet, not a token account: slashes go to any USDC account it
owns, so freezing or closing one account can't block an eviction.

fields.name: genesis_hash
docs: The cluster's genesis hash, bound into every settle ack. A program
cannot read the genesis hash on chain, so it is fixed at initialize.

fields.name: pending_admin
docs: Named by propose_admin and made admin when it signs accept_admin, so
a mistyped key never takes the admin seat. Default when none is
pending.

fields.name: _retired_min_grace
docs: Retired with max_grace.

fields.name: _retired_pending_arbiter
docs: Retired with the separate arbiter seat.

types.name: Node
docs: Zero-copy: every open and settle writes it, and borsh would re-serialize
the metrics ring each time. Field order keeps the struct free of padding.

fields.name: staging
docs: Advertised on chain but held out of normal routing.

fields.name: vault
docs: Stored so the hot path compares a key instead of re-deriving the PDA.

fields.name: operator
docs: The Operator PDA, stored for the same reason as `vault`.

fields.name: stake
docs: This node's share of the operator's stake: 0 for the first node.

fields.name: opens_total
docs: Every open takes the next value; the ticket keeps it as open_seq.

fields.name: settled_count
docs: Settled with the payer's ack, off chain or by `ack`.

fields.name: refunded_total
docs: Σ max_price of the tickets refunded inactive.

fields.name: latency_total_ms
docs: Σ ttft_ms over token-output settles; latency_samples is its divisor.

fields.name: ttft_ewma_ms
docs: 0 until the first token-output settle, which seeds it.

fields.name: decode_tps_ewma
docs: Output tokens per second; 0 until the first token settle with decode
time and output.

fields.name: revenue_total
docs: Σ amount charged, before the protocol fee.

fields.name: ring_day
docs: The day index (unix time / 86,400) of the latest ring write.

fields.name: protested_count
docs: Tickets the payer froze by protest, and Σ the amount their receipts
charged, each capped at its ticket's max_price: Algorand's
ticketsProtested and totalProtestedUsdc, which the SDKs show beside
the other metrics. Carved from the head of the reserve, so every
earlier offset stays put.

fields.name: frozen_dispute_count
docs: Tickets frozen by differing settle halves, whichever side posted
first, and Σ the amount the pending half named: Algorand's ticketsFrozenDispute and
totalFrozenDisputeUsdc. Carved from the head of the reserve.

fields.name: resolved_count
docs: Frozen tickets the admin's resolve_frozen ended, whatever the split,
and Σ the node's award (before the fee): Algorand's
ticketsResolvedAdmin and totalResolvedUsdc. Carved from the head of
the reserve.

types.name: Operator
docs: One per owner. Read-only on the hot path: open checks its status, and
nothing per-ticket writes it, so an operator's nodes never share a write
lane. That is why it carries no rolled-up metrics, unlike the Algorand
OperatorRecord; a reader sums the operator's nodes instead.

fields.name: next_node_id
docs: Starts at 1 and never goes back, so a removed node's id is never
reused.

fields.name: stake
docs: Micro-USDC this operator has in the stake vault, stored rather than
summed so it can be the slash base. It equals the operator stake paid
plus Σ live node.stake until a slash lowers it; node.stake is never
lowered, so unregister_node refunds at most this, and the operator's
unregister returns whatever remains.

fields.name: name_ref
docs: A name-service account the owner proved it holds; default when unset.

types.name: OperatorEvicted
docs: The admin's stated cause, kept on chain with the slash as Algorand keeps it
in the slash transfer's note.

types.name: RefundBumps
docs: The bump of the payer's ATA, computed off chain by whoever submits a
settle. The program then derives the address once instead of searching
for it, and a search's length depends on the payer's key, which the payer
can grind to push a node's settle past its compute limit.

types.name: RentPool
docs: A payer's prepaid ticket rent, as Algorand's per-payer MBR pool: open
draws each ticket's rent from it and every ending returns the rent here,
so a node never has its own lamports out on a payer's tickets. Rent
backing a live ticket sits in the ticket, so whatever the pool holds above
its own rent exemption is free to fund an open or to withdraw.

fields.name: open_tickets
docs: Live tickets this pool funded: Algorand's openTickets.
close_rent_pool waits for 0, so no ending returns rent to a closed
pool.

types.name: SetConfigArgs
docs: Each field left `None` keeps its current value. Stakes apply to later
registrations only, and fee and grace to later opens: a ticket keeps the
fee_bps and grace it opened with, and a stake is refunded as paid.

types.name: SettleOutcome
docs: How a ticket ended. Only the claim endings fold the claim into metrics.
Variants are appended, never reordered: the event encodes the index.

fields.name: open_seq
docs: Unique per open of this node. A closed ticket's address can be opened
again with the same ticket id, so the ack binds this, not the address
alone; otherwise an old ack replays against the new ticket.

fields.name: pending
docs: The first half's claim fields, all zero on an open ticket, as
Algorand's box keeps pendingAmount, pendingDigest and the rest: the
other side's half is compared with them, settle_lapsed pays them, and
a protest checks its receipt against their digest, so neither ending
needs a party to resupply them. A frozen ticket keeps them for whoever
resolves it.

fields.name: node_signing
docs: The node's signing key at open, which signs this ticket's receipt.
Settles check the node's current key instead, so a rotation retires a
leaked one at once (both rails, decided 2026-10-20). A protest must
check the receipt against this snapshot, as Algorand's protest checks
its ticket's nodeSigning: against the current key, a rotation would
void every protest of a receipt the old key signed.

fields.name: rent_payer
docs: Who funded the rent: the payer's rent pool, or the node's signer for
a ticket opened before pools existed. Closing the ticket refunds it
here, never to the caller, so a permissionless refund cannot capture
the rent.

fields.name: frozen_at
docs: When the ticket froze, and which path froze it (FREEZE_ORIGIN_*):
Algorand's frozenAt and freezeOrigin, for whoever resolves it. Zero
unless Frozen. Carved from the head of the reserve.

fields.name: ticket_id
docs: The id the address is derived from, which the address can't give
back. Everything off chain names a ticket by it (the wire, receipts,
the node's ledger, the payer's journal, protest's argument), so a walk
of a node's tickets can match each to those records and report it by
id, as an Algorand box walk can, the box's name being its ticket id.

fields.name: _reserve
docs: Smaller than the long-lived accounts' reserves: every live ticket's
rent is float the payer has out. A later field comes from here; a
Ticket grows past it only while no cluster holds a live ticket, since
Account<Ticket> refuses a shorter account before any handler can read
its `version`, which would lock the old tickets' escrow.

types.name: TicketClaimed
docs: A first half: the node's claim, or the payer's.

types.name: TicketDisputed
docs: A second half that differed from the first, which froze the ticket.

fields.name: claimed
docs: What the first half charged.

fields.name: amount
docs: What the second half charged.

types.name: TicketProtested
docs: Carries no payer: the ticket address names the dispute.

fields.name: amount
docs: What the protested receipt charged, read from the bytes the node
signed; on Algorand the payer asserts it beside the digest.

types.name: TicketResolved
docs: The admin's split of a frozen ticket, with its stated cause, as Algorand
keeps the reason as resolveFrozen's argument and on its payouts' notes.

types.name: TicketSettled
docs: Every way a ticket ends. Carries no payer and no model: the ticket address
names the ticket, and the payer appears only where the open's transfer
already put it on chain.

fields.name: refund_forfeited
docs: The payer's ATA couldn't take the refund, so it went to the treasury.

types.name: TicketStatus
docs: One enum rather than a status plus a separate "pending by" field, so an
open ticket cannot also name a claimant. Variants are appended, never
reordered: the account stores the index.

constants.name: RENT_POOL_SEED
docs: One rent pool per payer, seeded by the payer's key, so open finds the
pool from the payer it names and no one can fund a ticket from another
payer's pool.

constants.name: STAKE_VAULT_SEED
docs: Operator and node stakes sit in their own token account, which is its own
authority: only an instruction that signs with these seeds can move them,
so no escrow path can draw on stakes by mistake.

constants.name: TICKET_SEED
docs: Ticket PDAs are seeded by the node PDA as well as the ticket id. With a
global seed, a rival node that sees a ticket id broadcast could open it
first and squat it. The id is proto's wire ticket id, 16 bytes, so the
receipt a protest carries names the same id the ticket was opened with.
